name: Timbales
description: Historical recipe from The Canadian Family Cook Book (1914). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

instructions.text: Beat all together; let stand one hour.
Have ready a saucepan of boiling lard.
Put timbale-iron first in lard, then in batter and then in lard again for one-half minute, when the shells will fall off the iron readily.
Fill with creamed chicken and garnish with parsley or cress after heating a few moments in the oven.
The shells can be made the day before if desired and heated when required.

source.author: Grace E. Denison
source.originalInstructions:
1. Beat all together; let stand one hour.
2. Have ready a saucepan of boiling lard.
3. Put timbale-iron first in lard, then in batter and then in lard again for one-half minute, when the shells will fall off the iron readily.
4. Fill with creamed chicken and garnish with parsley or cress after heating a few moments in the oven.
5. The shells can be made the day before if desired and heated when required.
